description: Clear the captured Godot-MCP log cache (read by 'console-get-logs'). Useful for isolating logs to a specific action by clearing the slate first. NOTE: Godot's C# API exposes no managed hook to clear the editor's own Output panel, so (unlike Unity's analog) this clears only the MCP-side cache, not the Godot editor console window.
name: console-clear-logs
title: Console / Clear Logs

description:
Retrieve the Godot-MCP log lines captured in this process — the running game, where the in-game runtime (GodotMcpRuntime) registers this tool: newest-first by default, oldest-first when polling with 'sinceSequence'. To fetch only new lines, pass the highest 'sequence' you have received as 'sinceSequence'. The Godot analog of Unity's 'console-get-logs'. NOTE: Godot's C# API exposes no global log hook, so this returns what the plugin captured (its own GD.* routing, connection lifecycle diagnostics, and on Godot 4.5+ engine errors), not every line the game printed — an empty result is NOT evidence that the game printed nothing. For the game's errors (GDScript runtime errors, push_error, C# exceptions) prefer 'runtime-errors-get' (enable it with GodotMcpRuntime.Initialize(b => b.WithRuntimeErrorCapture())).
Inputs:
  - 'sinceSequence' (default 0, min 0): polling cursor. 0 = newest-first. > 0 = only lines with a higher sequence, oldest-first, so the next poll (with the highest sequence returned) continues where this page stopped. If returned sequences are lower than your cursor, the log restarted. Lines evicted from the 1000-line buffer or cleared before you poll are not returned.
  - 'maxEntries' (default 100, min 1): caps the returned array — the most recent lines at sinceSequence=0, the oldest page with a cursor.
  - 'logTypeFilter' (default null = all): restrict to Log / Warning / Error.
  - 'includeStackTrace' (default false): include stack-trace strings.
  - 'lastMinutes' (default 0 = all): only lines captured in the last N minutes.

description:
Call a C# method by reflection — including private methods. The Godot analog of Unity's 'reflection-method-call'. Requires a method schema obtained via 'reflection-method-find'. Supports static methods, instance methods (with optional target deserialization), and main-thread / off-thread execution.
Inputs:
  - 'targetObject' (optional) — for instance methods; { typeName, value } where value is deserialized to typeName. Null for static methods (or to construct a fresh instance). A Node target is written as { "typeName": "Godot.Control", "value": { "instanceId": 123 } } (or { "path": "/root/Main/Player" }); a Resource target as { "resourcePath": "res://x.tres" }.
  - 'inputParameters' (optional) — list of { typeName, name, value }; names/types are enhanced against the resolved signature when omitted.
  - 'executeInMainThread' (default true) — keep true for Godot-API-touching methods; set false only for thread-safe pure logic.
Godot.Variant parameters: A Godot.Variant is written either as a bare JSON scalar (null => Nil, true/false => Bool, integral number => Int, fractional number => Float, string => String) or as {"variantType":"<Type>","value":<json>} where <Type> is a Godot Variant.Type name. Composite types take a flat array of numbers in Godot's own constructor order (or, for Vector2/Vector2I/Vector3/Vector3I/Vector4/Vector4I/Quaternion/Plane/Color, an object with the named components): Vector2/Vector2I [x,y]; Vector3/Vector3I [x,y,z]; Vector4/Vector4I and Quaternion [x,y,z,w]; Color [r,g,b(,a)]; Plane [x,y,z,d] (the normal's xyz, then D); Rect2/Rect2I [x,y,width,height]; Aabb [x,y,z,width,height,depth]; Transform2D [xx,xy,yx,yy,ox,oy]; Basis [xx,yx,zx,xy,yy,zy,xz,yz,zz]; Transform3D = Basis then [ox,oy,oz]; Projection = four Vector4 columns flattened (16). String/StringName/NodePath take a string. Array takes a JSON array of variants (each a bare scalar or an envelope); Dictionary takes a JSON object of String keys or an array of {"key":<variant>,"value":<variant>}; Packed*Array takes a flat array of its element values (numbers, strings, or component arrays for the vector/color kinds); Object takes {"resourcePath":"res://..."} or {"instanceId":N} (null clears it). Note: a parameter DECLARED as a concrete type (e.g. 'Godot.Vector3') keeps its own member-wise shape ({"x":1,"y":2,"z":3}); only a 'Godot.Variant' parameter uses this envelope — and its named-component object form matches that member-wise shape, so the same value can be written either way.
An argument whose value cannot be read is an ERROR — the method is never invoked with a silently defaulted argument.

description:
Change the live Godot editor with an RQL query whose last stage is set or call. All-or-nothing: every target and value is checked before anything is written; a failure changes nothing. Undoable in the editor (Ctrl+Z). Scene edits mark the scene unsaved (save with editor | call SaveScene()); edited resource files (res://….tres) are saved to disk automatically. dry_run=true returns the receipt ($ref, member, old, new) without changing anything. Do exactly the change requested; a read-only member fails with readonly-member instead of being approximated.
  set path = expr, ...   assign members (paths may go through structs: set Position.Y = Position.Y + 1); values see each target: $ and $index (its position in the stream entering set / call)
  call Method(args)   invoke a method the tools expose
Examples:
  nodes | where name == "Player" | set Position = "(0, 1, 0)"   move a node
  nodes | where class == "OmniLight3D" | set props["light_energy"] = props["light_energy"] * 2, props["light_color"] = "#ffcc88"   Godot properties by their snake_case name
  nodes | where name starts-with "Enemy" | set Visible = false   hide every enemy
  nodes | where name starts-with "Enemy" | sort name | set Position.X = $index * 2   spread the matches along X
  godot.resource("res://materials/red.tres") | set props["albedo_color"] = "(1, 0, 0, 1)"   edit a resource file (saved to disk)
  root | call AddChild("Node3D", "Props")   new child node of a class; the receipt's result column holds its $ref
  nodes | where name == "Props" | call InstantiateScene("res://scenes/enemy.tscn")   instance a scene as a child
  nodes | where name == "Crate" | call Duplicate()   copy next to it (returns the copy)
  nodes | where name == "Floor" | set Mesh = {$type: "PlaneMesh", Size: "(20, 20)"}   a new embedded resource (mesh, shape, material, environment …) of a concrete class, with its members; a script class_name works too
  nodes | where name == "Crate" | call Reparent(godot.find("Props"))   reparent (keeps the global transform)
  nodes | where name == "Crate" | call MoveChild(0)   reorder among its siblings (-1 = last)
  nodes | where name == "Old" | call Free()   remove a node (undoable, like Delete in the Scene dock)
  editor | set selection = [godot.find("Player")]   change the editor selection
  editor | call SaveScene()   write the edited scene to its .tscn
  editor | call CreateResource("res://materials/blue.tres", "StandardMaterial3D")   new resource file (a Godot class or a script class_name)
  editor | call MoveResource("res://materials/blue.tres", "res://materials/old/blue.tres")   move / rename a file (its .import / .uid sidecars move with it)
  editor | call DeleteResource("res://materials/old/blue.tres")   delete a file and its sidecars
  editor | call NewScene("res://scenes/new.tscn", "Node2D", "Main")   create, save and open a scene (path, root class, root name)
  editor | call OpenScene("res://scenes/level.tscn")   open a scene file
  editor | call Reimport(["res://materials/red.tres"])   re-import files (no argument: full filesystem scan)
  editor | call ClearConsole()   clear the captured editor log
  nodes | where name starts-with "Enemy" | call AddToGroup("enemies")   add nodes to a group (saved with the scene; set groups = [...] replaces them)
  nodes | where name == "Enemy1" | call Connect("tree_exited", godot.find("Player"), "_on_enemy_died")   connect a signal to a method of the target's script (saved with the scene)
  nodes | where name == "Enemy1" | get connections | where method == "_on_enemy_died" | call Disconnect()   remove a connection
  project | set settings["display/window/size/viewport_width"] = 1280   any project setting by its path (saved to project.godot)
  project | call AddInputAction("jump", ["Key:Space", "JoypadButton:A"])   new input action with its events
  inputActions | where name == "jump" | call AddEvent("Key:W")   add an event to an input action (RemoveEvent, set events = [...], set deadzone)
  project | call AddAutoload("Game", "res://scenes/game.gd")   register an autoload singleton
  godot.resource("res://tiles/terrain.tres") | call AddAtlasSource("res://tiles/terrain.png")   add a texture to a TileSet (returns the source id)
  godot.resource("res://tiles/terrain.tres") | get sources | get atlas | call CreateTilesFromTexture()   create tiles in the non-transparent grid cells
  godot.resource("res://ui/theme.tres") | set colors["Button/font_color"] = "#ffcc00", constants["HBoxContainer/separation"] = 8   edit Theme items
  layers | where kind == "3d_physics" and index == 2 | set name = "enemies"   name a layer (saved to project.godot)
  nodes | where name == "Wall" | set layerNames["collision_mask"] = [1, "enemies"]   a layer mask by layer names (numbers for unnamed layers)
  godot.resource("res://materials/water.tres") | set params["speed"] = 2, params["tint"] = "#3388ff"   shader uniforms of a ShaderMaterial (null or call ClearParam(name) reverts one)
  godot.resource("res://meshes/tiles.tres") | call CreateItem("Floor", "res://meshes/floor.tres")   add a MeshLibrary item (set its shapes, navigationMesh … on the returned row)
  nodes | where class == "OmniLight3D" | set name = name.replace("Lamp", "Light")   bulk rename (replace, replace-regex, substring, pad …)
  files | where path == "res://tiles/terrain.png" | set importSettings["mipmaps/generate"] = true   change an import option (re-imports the file; a .wav loops with edit/loop_mode = 2)
Editor state: editor | set isPlaying = true / false runs / stops the main scene; editor | call PlayScene("res://…") runs one scene; what the game prints and its errors: rql-query gameLog. editor | call Undo() / Redo() steps the editor's undo history like Ctrl+Z (returns the action; rql-query editor | select undoHistory lists the scene's and the global history); editor | call ReloadScene() reloads the edited scene from its file; NewScene(path, "res://base.tscn") makes an inherited scene.
Object literals build values: set Position = {x: 1, y: 2, z: 3}; {$type: "PlaneMesh"} picks a concrete class. Map entries streamed by get write through their map: … | get colors | where Key starts-with "Button/" | set Value = "#ffffff". Up to 200 targets per call; for an intended bulk change of more objects pass max_targets = the match count (at most 1000): still one all-or-nothing, undoable call. Nodes inside a scene instance take property changes (saved as overrides; the instance gets Editable Children) but are removed, renamed or moved in their own scene.

Query part: the RQL of rql-query (full guide and the sources in its description); godot.resources("Texture2D"), godot.resource(path), godot.find("Name"), ref("Node3D#1234"). Stages: where, select, sort, first N, get <path>, recurse children. Operators: == != < > and or not, contains, starts-with, $ is Node3D, cond ? a : b. Paths a.b.c, list[0], props["key"]. Vectors/colors as "(1, 2, 3)" or "#ff8800"; enums as strings.

dry_run.description: true = preview the receipt without changing anything

max_targets.description: Most objects the set / call stage may change (default 200, at most 1000). Raise it to the match count for an intended bulk change of more objects: the call stays all-or-nothing and one undo step.

query.description: RQL query ending with a set or call stage, e.g. nodes | where name == "Player" | set Visible = false

name: rql-mutate
title: RQL / Mutate

description:
Run a read-only RQL query against the live Godot editor and return compact rows. One precise query beats many exploratory calls. Changes need rql-mutate.

RQL: source | stage | stage ...
Sources: nodes (every node of the edited scene, depth-first, root included), root (the edited scene root), selection, scenes (open scenes), files (every res:// file the editor knows; on request deps, missingDeps, usedBy (scenes / resources that load it) and importSettings["option"]), classes (Godot classes, ClassDB), console (captured editor log entries), gameLog (what the game run from the editor printed: Sequence LogType Message StackTrace), editor (editor state, undoHistory / redoHistory, and operations), project (project settings: settings["section/key"], name, mainScene; input map, autoload and global group calls), settings (every project setting: name section value type changed), inputActions (name events deadzone builtIn), autoloads (name path singleton order), groups (name nodes count global), layers (kind index name: the project's layer names). Resources: godot.resources("StandardMaterial3D") or godot.resources("Texture2D", "res://art"), godot.resource("res://materials/red.tres"). ref("Node3D#1234") resolves a $ref; godot.find("Player") or godot.find("Level/Player") a node by unique name or path below the scene root; godot.group("enemies") the nodes of a group; godot.callable("Player", "_on_hit") a Callable.
Stages:
  where <predicate>   filter
  select a b.c alias=(expr)   project columns (wrap computed expressions in parentheses)
  sort <expr> [desc], ...   stable sort
  first N | skip N | count
  get <path>   replace each item by a member (lists are flattened)
  recurse children [max-depth=N] [include-self=false]   walk the scene tree (input items included by default)
  distinct [expr] | sum expr | min expr | max expr | avg expr
  group-by expr   rows key|count; group-by a, b (or kind=class) gives one column per key, then count
Expressions: == != < <= > >= and or not + - * / %; contains, starts-with, ends-with (case-insensitive); matches "regex"; x in [a, b]; x is null; x is not null; $ is Node3D (includes subclasses); has(member). Conditional: cond ? a : b or if(cond, a, b) (only the taken branch runs; inside select wrap it in parentheses: select name kind=($ is MeshInstance3D ? "mesh" : "other")). Text: replace(s, from, to) (case-insensitive), replace-regex(s, pattern, repl) ($1 = group 1), substring(s, start[, length]), split(s, sep), trim(s), pad(v, width[, fill]) — also as methods: name.replace("Old", "New"), name.substring(0, 4). Literals: numbers, "strings", true/false/null, lists [a, b], objects {x: 1, y: 2}.
Paths: a.b.c, list[0], map["key"]; .member on a list maps over its elements. List methods: .any(pred) .all(pred) .count([pred]) .sum(e) .min(e) .max(e) .first([pred]); inside them bare names refer to the element, falling back to the outer item.
Meta: $ (current item), $ref (stable id such as Node3D#1234), $type, $path, $index, $depth. Enums compare to strings; == on strings is case-sensitive.
Godot: every node has name, path (below the scene root, "." = root), class (the Godot class, e.g. "OmniLight3D"), parent, owner, children (list), childCount, index, script (res:// path), groups (list) and id; signals, connections (persistent: signal target method flags), incoming and overrides (how a scene instance differs from its scene file: node property value template) are read on request (select connections, get overrides). Members are the C# properties (Position, Rotation, Scale, Visible, Text …), matched case-insensitively, so position works too; Rotation is in radians, RotationDegrees in degrees. Every Godot property, including GDScript script variables (in the editor: @export ones, every one of a @tool script) and GDExtension properties, is in props["snake_name"] (e.g. props["light_energy"], props["speed"] on a scripted node); a Godot array lists the values it holds (get props["items"] | where props["price"] > 10). Vectors / colors print as (x, y, z); write "(1, 2, 3)", [1, 2, 3] or {x: 1, y: 2, z: 3}; colors also "#ff8800". A resource path "res://…" works wherever a resource is expected, a node path or name wherever a node is expected. Freed nodes read as null. Input events are text: "Key:Space", "Key:Ctrl+S", "PhysicalKey:W", "Mouse:Left", "JoypadButton:A", "JoypadMotion:LeftX-". A TileSet has sources (id kind atlas texture tileCount), physicsLayers, terrainSets, customDataLayers; an atlas source has tiles (coords size data). A Theme has maps keyed "ControlType/item": colors, constants, fonts, fontSizes, icons, styleboxes. A ShaderMaterial has uniforms (name type default value overridden) and params["uniform"] (typed by the shader; null reverts to the default); a MeshLibrary has items (id name mesh meshTransform shapes navigationMesh preview). Layer masks by name: layerNames["collision_mask"] on any object with layer properties is a list of layer names (a number for an unnamed layer). Callables are "Player::_on_hit" (target::method); RIDs are read-only "RID(…)"; a Projection is 16 numbers. Navigate with paths or get; select only projects output columns.
Results come back as compact rows (header line, then col|col). Long results are truncated — refine with where/first or use count. Unknown members produce warnings with suggestions (in rql-mutate a misspelt member that leaves no target is an error); rql-schema(type) lists a type's members and Godot properties.

Examples:
  nodes | where name contains "Enemy" | select $ref name class path
  nodes | where $ is Node3D and Position.Y > 0 | select name Position
  nodes | where class == "OmniLight3D" | select name props["light_energy"] props["light_color"]
  root | recurse children | where childCount == 0 | select path class
  godot.resources("StandardMaterial3D") | select path props["albedo_color"]
  files | where ext == "tscn" | select path
  scenes | select name path active
  classes | where parent == "Light3D" | select name
  console | where logType == "Error" | sort sequence desc | first 5 | select message
  editor | select isPlaying editedScene selection
  godot.group("enemies") | select name path
  nodes | where name == "Player" | get incoming | select source signal method
  settings | where section == "display" and changed | select name value
  inputActions | where builtIn == false | select name events
  autoloads | select name path singleton
  godot.resources("TileSet") | get sources | select id kind texture tileCount
  godot.resource("res://materials/water.tres") | get uniforms | select name type default value overridden
  nodes | where class == "StaticBody3D" | select name layerNames["collision_layer"] layerNames["collision_mask"]
  layers | where kind == "3d_physics" and name != "" | select index name
  godot.resources("MeshLibrary") | get items | select id name mesh
  nodes | group-by class, scripted=(script is not null)
  nodes | where $ is Node3D | select name kind=($ is MeshInstance3D ? "mesh" : $ is Light3D ? "light" : "other")
  files | where type contains "Material" and usedBy.count() == 0 | select path
  files | where missingDeps.count() > 0 | select path missingDeps
  nodes | where SceneFilePath != "" and overrides.count() > 0 | select name overrides
  editor | select undoHistory redoHistory

title: RQL / Query

description: Without a type: RQL sources, functions, and the node classes present in the edited scene (with counts), plus the Node members. With a type name (e.g. "Node3D", "OmniLight3D", "StandardMaterial3D", "Vector3", "editor"): that type's members (name type; ro = read-only), methods, and its Godot properties (props["name"]). Use it before querying an unfamiliar class.
name: rql-schema
title: RQL / Schema

description: Clear the captured in-game runtime-error buffer (read by 'runtime-errors-get'). Useful for isolating errors to a specific in-game action by clearing the slate first, then performing the action, then polling 'runtime-errors-get'. NOTE: the monotonic sequence counter is NOT reset, so a 'sinceSequence' poll from before the clear still behaves correctly (no old rows reappear). A no-op when runtime error capture is not enabled in this game.
name: runtime-errors-clear
title: Runtime Errors / Clear

description:
Retrieve errors raised inside the RUNNING game — GDScript runtime errors, push_error/push_warning, shader errors (Godot 4.5+ engine hook), and C# unhandled / unobserved-Task exceptions (with full managed stack traces). This is the in-game counterpart to the editor's 'script-validate' and RQL 'console' source: it lets an agent driving a live game detect real gameplay/runtime bugs instead of assuming the game is healthy because the editor console is quiet.
Poll loop: pass the 'highestSequence' from the previous call as 'sinceSequence' to get ONLY newer errors. Start with sinceSequence=0 (default) for everything captured so far.
Inputs:
  - 'sinceSequence' (default 0): return only errors with a sequence number greater than this.
  - 'maxEntries' (default 100, min 1): cap the returned page (newest kept; 'truncated' flags a cap).
Result (RuntimeErrorsResult): 'available' (false when the game did not enable runtime error capture — then an empty list proves nothing), 'ok' (no error-severity entries), the 'errors' [{ sequence, message, type, source, file, line, function, stackTrace, frames, timestamp }] oldest-first, counts, 'highestSequence' (poll with it next), and a 'truncated' flag. On Godot 4.5+ a GDScript runtime error also carries 'frames' (the deep multi-frame call stack, innermost-first, each { function, file, line }) and a formatted 'stackTrace'.
SECURITY: messages and stack traces are forwarded verbatim and may contain sensitive runtime data (absolute filesystem paths, machine/user names, or a secret that appeared in an exception). Capture is OFF by default and the developer must enable it via WithRuntimeErrorCapture(); enable it only on a trusted loopback + token connection.

maxEntries.description: Maximum number of errors to return. Minimum 1, default 100. Newest kept when capped.

sinceSequence.description: Return only errors with a sequence number greater than this. Pass the previous result's 'highestSequence' to poll only new errors. Default 0 (all captured).

name: runtime-errors-get

items.description: A single captured in-game runtime error: message, type, origin (file/line/function), source, an optional managed stack trace, a monotonic sequence number, and a UTC timestamp.
One frame of a captured script-language (e.g. GDScript) backtrace: function, file, line.

com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Data.RuntimeErr.description: A single captured in-game runtime error: message, type, origin (file/line/function), source, an optional managed stack trace, a monotonic sequence number, and a UTC timestamp.

file.description: Origin file of an engine error (e.g. 'res://scripts/player.gd'); empty for managed faults (the origin is in the stack trace instead).

frames.description: Structured deep backtrace for a Godot 4.5+ engine GDScript error: ordered stack frames (innermost-first), each with function / file / line. Null for managed C# faults (their stack is in 'stackTrace') and for engine errors with no tracked backtrace (Godot < 4.5 or release builds without call-stack tracking).

function.description: Origin function of an engine error; empty when unknown / for managed faults.

line.description: 1-based origin line of an engine error, or -1 when unknown / for managed faults.

sequence.description: Monotonic 1-based sequence number assigned when captured. Pass the largest you have seen as 'sinceSequence' to 'runtime-errors-get' to poll only NEWER errors.

source.description: Where the error came from: Engine (Godot error stream) / UnhandledException / UnobservedTaskException (managed C# faults with a full stack trace).

stackTrace.description: Stack trace string: for a C# fault (UnhandledException / UnobservedTaskException) the full managed stack; for a Godot 4.5+ engine GDScript error the formatted multi-frame backtrace (see 'frames'); null for engine errors with no tracked backtrace (Godot < 4.5 or release builds without call-stack tracking).

timestamp.description: UTC timestamp when the error was captured.

type.description: The error type/severity: for engine errors one of Error / Warning / Script / Shader; for managed faults the CLR exception type name (e.g. 'System.NullReferenceException').

com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Data.RuntimeErr.description: One frame of a captured script-language (e.g. GDScript) backtrace: function, file, line.

file.description: The source file of this stack frame's call site (e.g. 'res://scripts/player.gd'); empty when the engine omitted it.

function.description: The function called at this stack frame (e.g. '_process'); empty when the engine omitted it.

line.description: The 1-based line number of this stack frame's call site, or -1 when unknown.

com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Data.RuntimeErr.description: Result of 'runtime-errors-get': whether capture is available, the captured runtime errors newer than the requested sequence, counts, and the highest sequence seen (poll with it next time).

available.description: True when in-game runtime error capture is wired up (the runtime was initialized with capture enabled). When false, the runtime was never started with capture, so an empty 'errors' list proves nothing — enable capture via GodotMcpRuntime's WithRuntimeErrorCapture().

count.description: Number of runtime errors returned in 'errors' (after the 'sinceSequence' filter and the 'maxEntries' cap).

errorCount.description: Number of error-severity entries in 'errors' (managed faults + engine Error/Script/Shader).

errors.description: The captured runtime errors newer than 'sinceSequence', oldest-first within the page so they read in chronological order. Empty when 'ok' is true / capture is unavailable.

highestSequence.description: The highest sequence number across ALL captured runtime errors (not just the returned page). Pass this as 'sinceSequence' on the next call to poll only newer errors. 0 when none have ever been captured.

note.description: Human-readable summary, e.g. 'No new runtime errors (capture active).' or '2 runtime error(s) since sequence 5.' or 'Runtime error capture is not enabled in this game.'.

ok.description: True when no error-severity runtime errors are present in 'errors' (warnings do not flip this to false). Always true when capture is unavailable or the buffer is empty.

truncated.description: True when more matching errors existed than the 'maxEntries' cap returned. The NEWEST are kept; call again (the buffer is bounded, so very old errors may already have been evicted).

warningCount.description: Number of warning-severity entries in 'errors' (engine Warning).

result.description: Result of 'runtime-errors-get': whether capture is available, the captured runtime errors newer than the requested sequence, counts, and the highest sequence seen (poll with it next time).

title: Runtime Errors / Get

description: Capture a screenshot from a specific Camera3D (or Camera2D) in the edited scene and return it as a PNG image for direct LLM inspection. Identify the camera with 'nodeRef' (instanceId preferred, else a scene-tree path). The camera's own world is rendered into a temporary off-screen SubViewport at the requested 'width'x'height', so the editor's live selection/camera is left untouched. Output edges are capped to keep the response transportable. NOTE: rendering needs a real GPU — a Godot launched with '--headless' yields an empty image, surfaced here as a structured error rather than a blank PNG.

com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Data.NodeRef.description: Reference to a Godot Node in the scene tree, located by scene-tree path or instance id.

instanceId.description: Instance id of the Node (Godot GodotObject.GetInstanceId()). If '0', treated as unset. Priority: 1.

path.description: Scene-tree path of the Node, e.g. '/root/Main/Player' or 'Main/Player'. Priority: 2.

height.description: Output height in pixels. Default 1080. Must be > 0 and within the dimension cap.

nodeRef.description: Reference to the camera Node (Camera3D or Camera2D) to capture from (instanceId preferred, else scene-tree path).

width.description: Output width in pixels. Default 1920. Must be > 0 and within the dimension cap.

name: screenshot-camera
title: Screenshot / Camera

description: Render a target Node3D in ISOLATION (only the target is visible, in its own world) from a chosen camera angle, framed automatically to its bounding box, lit by a default directional light, and return the result as a PNG image for direct LLM inspection. Identify the target with 'nodeRef'. Choose the view with 'cameraView' (Front/Back/Left/Right/Top/Bottom). Pick a 'background' (SolidColor or Transparent) and, for SolidColor, a hex 'backgroundColor'. The target is rendered via a temporary off-screen copy, so the edited scene is never mutated. Output is a square 'resolution'x'resolution' PNG, capped to keep the response transportable. NOTE: rendering needs a real GPU — a Godot launched with '--headless' yields an empty image, surfaced here as a structured error rather than a blank PNG.

com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Data.NodeRef.description: Reference to a Godot Node in the scene tree, located by scene-tree path or instance id.

instanceId.description: Instance id of the Node (Godot GodotObject.GetInstanceId()). If '0', treated as unset. Priority: 1.

path.description: Scene-tree path of the Node, e.g. '/root/Main/Player' or 'Main/Player'. Priority: 2.

background.description: Background mode for the render: SolidColor (default) or Transparent.

backgroundColor.description: Hex background color (e.g. '#404040'). Used only when background is SolidColor.

cameraView.description: Camera angle relative to the target's bounding box. Default: Front.

fieldOfView.description: Camera vertical field of view in degrees. Default: 60.

nodeRef.description: Reference to the target Node3D to render in isolation (instanceId preferred, else path).

padding.description: Framing multiplier around the object. 1.0 = tight fit, 1.5 = 50% extra space. Default: 1.2.

resolution.description: Output image resolution in pixels (width = height). Default: 512.

name: screenshot-isolated
title: Screenshot / Isolated Node

description: Capture the Godot editor's main viewport (the 3D or 2D editing surface) and return it as a PNG image for direct LLM inspection. Set 'mode' to '3d' (default) for the 3D editor viewport or '2d' for the 2D editor viewport. The longest output edge is capped to keep the response transportable; oversized captures are scaled down (aspect preserved). NOTE: the viewport must have a live GPU render — a Godot launched with '--headless' has no rendering device and yields an empty image, which surfaces here as a structured error rather than a blank PNG.

mode.description: Which editor viewport to capture: '3d' (the 3D editor surface, default) or '2d' (the 2D editor surface). Case-insensitive.

name: screenshot-viewport
title: Screenshot / Editor Viewport

description: Attach a script (C# '.cs' or GDScript '.gd') to a Node in the currently edited Godot scene — the Godot analog of adding a MonoBehaviour to a GameObject. Identify the target with 'nodeRef' (instanceId preferred, else scene-tree path) and the script with 'scriptPath' (a res:// script file that must exist). Pass an empty/whitespace/null 'scriptPath' to DETACH (clear) the node's script. The script resource is loaded and set via Node.SetScript; the scene is marked unsaved (persist with rql-mutate 'editor | call SaveScene()'). Returns the script's structured ScriptInfo on attach, or an identity record with a 'detached' status on clear.

description: Build the project's C# (dotnet build, Debug configuration like the editor's builds) so C# scripts written with 'script-create' / 'script-update' load: new [GlobalClass] types, changed node scripts. The build runs in the background; when it succeeds Godot reloads the C# assembly and the plugin reconnects, and the result (the warning count, or the compiler errors) is delivered after that reload through the request's requestId. Tool calls made while the reload is pending are refused with a retryable error: retry them a few seconds later.

title: Script / Build

description: Create a NEW Godot script file (C# '.cs' or GDScript '.gd') under res:// with the provided source. Fails if a file already exists at the path — use 'script-update' to overwrite. GDScript content is syntax-validated before write (invalid '.gd' is rejected and nothing is written); C# is accepted as-is (no in-editor compiler) and the post-write build settle surfaces compile errors. Missing parent directories are created. For a '.cs' file the editor filesystem reimports and BOUNDED-settles before returning (then 'script-build' builds the project and loads the new type); a '.gd' file only needs a filesystem update. Returns a structured ScriptInfo.

content.description: Source code for the new script file.

scriptPath.description: res:// path for the new script, ending in '.cs' (C#) or '.gd' (GDScript), e.g. 'res://scripts/Enemy.cs' or 'res://scripts/player.gd'.

description: Delete a Godot script file (C# '.cs' or GDScript '.gd') from the res:// filesystem. Fails if no file exists at the path. The script's identity (path, language) is captured BEFORE deletion and returned for confirmation. The file is removed with DirAccess, along with its Godot '.uid' sidecar when present, then the editor filesystem is rescanned and (for a '.cs' file) BOUNDED-settles. WARNING: nodes/resources referencing the deleted script will break — verify with 'script-read' first. A loaded copy is detached from the path, so an open scene still using it embeds it on its next save. Returns a structured ScriptInfo.

scriptPath.description: res:// path of the script file to delete, ending in '.cs' or '.gd'.

description: Compiles and runs C# in the Godot editor: plain statements with the last expression as the result (own usings, local classes, await allowed), or a declared class 'className' with static method 'methodName'. Returns the result and the printed output (Console; GD.Print on Godot 4.5+).

fields.description: Fields of the object, serialized as a list of 'SerializedMember'.

props.description: Properties of the object, serialized as a list of 'SerializedMember'.

value.description: Value of the object, serialized as a non stringified JSON element. Can be null if the value is not set. Can be default value if the value is an empty object or array json.

Snippet: 'var root = EditorInterface.Singleton.GetEditedSceneRoot();\nroot.GetChildCount()' (System, LINQ and Godot are imported; the last expression is the result, so no ';' after it). Full: 'using Godot;\npublic class Script { public static int Main() { return 42; } }' (full code brings its own usings).

parameters.description: Parameters, each with 'name' and 'typeName': the snippet's variables or the method's arguments in order. Leave empty when none.

usings.description: Extra namespaces for snippet mode, e.g. ["MyGame.Gameplay"].

description: Read a Godot script file (C# '.cs' or GDScript '.gd') under res:// and return its content + metadata (res:// path, language, line count). Supports an optional 1-based 'lineFrom'/'lineTo' slice for partial reads (indices are clamped — out-of-range values read at-most the whole file). Pair with 'script-update'/'script-create' to write back. The file is read with Godot's FileAccess so it works on any res:// path (imported or not). Returns a structured ScriptInfo.

lineTo.description: 1-based inclusive end line of the slice (default -1 = end of file). Clamped into range.

description:
Validate GDScript ('.gd') files and return STRUCTURED parse/compile diagnostics — the on-demand 'is the project error-free?' query. Closes the gap where the agent gets NO feedback on GDScript parse errors and assumes the game runs fine.
Inputs:
  - 'scriptPath' (optional): a single res:// '.gd' path to validate. Omit to scan every '.gd' under res:// (capped at FullScanFileCap).
Result (ScriptDiagnosticsResult): 'ok' (true when no errors), 'diagnostics' [{ path, line, message, severity }], counts, a 'truncated' flag (true when a full scan hit the file cap, so 'ok' is NOT a whole-project all-clear), and a 'fidelity' note:
  - Godot 4.5+: 'Precise' — exact line + message captured via the engine Logger hook.
  - Godot < 4.5: 'Coarse' — per-file pass/fail with the engine error code (no line/message text).
C# ('.cs') files are NOT validated here (Godot has no in-editor C# compiler to reach cheaply); their compile errors surface through the project build. Pair with the RQL 'console' source (rql-query 'console | where logType == "Error"'), which on Godot 4.5+ also captures engine GDScript parse errors passively.

scriptPath.description: Optional single res:// '.gd' script path to validate, e.g. 'res://scripts/player.gd'. Omit (null/empty) to scan every '.gd' file under res://.

name: script-validate

items.description: A single script diagnostic (parse/compile error or warning): the res:// path, 1-based line (-1 when unknown), message, and severity.

com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Data.ScriptDiag.description: A single script diagnostic (parse/compile error or warning): the res:// path, 1-based line (-1 when unknown), message, and severity.

line.description: 1-based source line of the diagnostic, or -1 when the live Godot version cannot report a line (Godot < 4.5 falls back to a per-file error code with no line).

message.description: Human-readable diagnostic text (Godot 4.5+), or the engine Error code name (e.g. 'ParseError') on older versions where the message text is not reachable.

path.description: res:// path of the script the diagnostic belongs to, e.g. 'res://scripts/player.gd'.

com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Data.ScriptDiag.description: Result of 'script-validate': an Ok verdict, the scanned script paths, captured diagnostics, and a fidelity note about how precise the diagnostics are on the live Godot version.

diagnostics.description: The captured diagnostics (errors first, then warnings). Empty when 'ok' is true.

fidelity.description: How precise the diagnostics are on the live Godot version: 'Precise' (4.5+: line + message captured) or 'Coarse' (Godot < 4.5: per-file pass/fail with the engine error code, no line).

note.description: Human-readable summary, e.g. 'No script errors found (12 scanned).' or '2 errors in 1 script.'. Includes a fidelity caveat on older Godot versions and a truncation hint when the full-scan cap was hit.

ok.description: True when no error-severity diagnostics were found across every scanned script.

scannedCount.description: Number of script files that were validated.

scannedPaths.description: res:// paths of the script files that were validated.

truncated.description: True when a full-project scan hit the file cap and only the first N '.gd' files were validated — so 'ok' is NOT a guaranteed all-clear for the whole project. Validate a specific 'scriptPath' (or sub-tree) to cover the rest. Always false for a single-path validation.

result.description: Result of 'script-validate': an Ok verdict, the scanned script paths, captured diagnostics, and a fidelity note about how precise the diagnostics are on the live Godot version.

title: Script / Validate
